answers.text: Making things, having time to myself, a few people I trust. Maybe engineering or repair work. I do not need my hobby to become my job. I want to be good at something useful.
People sometimes hear me being rude when I am asking for the missing information. I have been told that. I do care about them. I just do not always know what they want me to say.
A problem I can work out. I repaired an old speaker because I wanted to know why it stopped working. I struggle with tasks where the instructions change but nobody explains why.
I like seeing a friend, then I need space. Groups wear me out if lots of conversations happen at once. I can talk for ages to someone about a shared interest.
I speak if I think I can move it forward. In robotics I proposed a way to test two designs. I was happy for someone else to present. I do not need to be in charge of the whole group.
I compare what each option would actually involve. I changed a school subject after reading the course outline and talking to the teacher. I wanted something I would still want to do a year later.
I read a bit then try. I like unfamiliar problems, less so unfamiliar social events. A climbing route can be interesting because my first solution fails and I have to work out another.
A clear sequence helps. I like knowing what done means. If the method fails I will change the method. When our robotics part broke I used a different connection, but I kept the same test plan.
If there is a reason I keep at it. If I am repeating something that does not work I want to change it. I stopped an online course because it was mostly things I already knew.
I look for a diagram, manual or example and then ask a person who knows. I posted a clear question about the speaker repair with a photo. Someone pointed out a connection I had missed.
Say what is wrong and what the result needs to be. I can use that. Hints like you know what I mean are hard. I do not always know. A teacher writing it down helped.
Short answers. I may leave the conversation. I usually know I need time but I do not always say it. Once a friend thought I was angry with them when I was frustrated with the project.

I ask what we disagree about. In robotics someone said I was dismissing their idea. I thought we were comparing designs. I asked them to explain and then suggested we test both. I do not know if they felt fully heard.
A clear account of what happened. I did not finish a route and wrote down the bit I could not solve. Later I tried a different approach. I also sometimes just want to go home.
I can separate a big problem into smaller tests. I find useful information and share it. I ask who wants to do which part because doing all of it myself takes too long.
I can keep searching for an exact explanation when we only need a workable one. I spent too long comparing parts and we nearly missed an order deadline. Someone pointed out the time and I picked.
Clear words and taking my answer seriously. I try not to pretend I agree. I can forget that a person might want me to listen before I suggest a solution.
I get more exact and less talkative. If people keep asking several questions I lose track. With one problem and time to think I am usually okay. It depends on how many things are happening.
Noise and being expected to answer instantly. A quiet walk or working alone on something small. My week is okay at the moment. I still need unplanned time even though I like plans.
I change my mind when a test shows something different. Being organised does not mean I hate change. Also I make terrible jokes with my friends. I do not talk like a manual all the time.

questions.prompt: What matters most to you outside sport?
questions.followup: What would you like your life to make room for, now or later?

questions.prompt: What do people sometimes get wrong about you?
questions.followup: What would they understand better if they heard your side?

questions.prompt: What makes you want to put effort into something?
questions.followup: Tell us about something you chose to do, and something you found hard to care about.

questions.prompt: After spending time with other people, how do you usually feel?
questions.followup: Is it different with close friends and an unfamiliar group?

questions.prompt: In a group, how do you usually get involved?
questions.followup: When do you speak up, choose a direction, or leave room for someone else?

questions.prompt: When a choice is difficult, how do you decide?
questions.followup: Think of a recent choice. What mattered, and how long did you need?

questions.prompt: How do you approach something new or unfamiliar?
questions.followup: What makes you curious, and what makes you hold back?

questions.prompt: How much of a plan do you like before you start?
questions.followup: What happened the last time your plan changed?

questions.prompt: When something gets boring or difficult, what do you do?
questions.followup: Describe a time you kept going, changed your approach, or decided to stop.

questions.prompt: When you do not understand something, what do you try?
questions.followup: What happened the last time? Did another person or a tool help?

questions.prompt: What kind of feedback is easiest for you to use?
questions.followup: Describe feedback that helped, and anything that made it harder to take in.

questions.prompt: When you are upset, what might someone else notice?
questions.followup: What might they miss? Only tell us what you want to share.

questions.prompt: When you disagree with someone, what usually happens?
questions.followup: Can you remember an example, including what the other person actually said or did?

questions.prompt: After a disappointment, what helps you find your footing?
questions.followup: What happened on one occasion? It is okay if you are still figuring this out.

questions.prompt: What do you bring to a group that is useful?
questions.followup: Think of school, home, friends or sport. How do you share the work?

questions.prompt: When can one of your strengths get in your way?
questions.followup: How do you notice it, and is there a situation where it works differently?

questions.prompt: What makes you feel respected or fairly treated?
questions.followup: How do you try to offer that to someone else?

questions.prompt: What changes about you when the pressure rises?
questions.followup: Compare an ordinary situation with a difficult one. What was going on around you?

questions.prompt: What drains you, and what helps you feel like yourself again?
questions.followup: Is anything about your current week making a difference?

questions.prompt: What else should MORE understand about you?
questions.followup: Where have your answers missed the full picture? What are you still figuring out?
